items.title: Albert "June" Gardner Interview, 1996-04-17
items.q: These guys would make a roll and it would be like you're tearing paper. And I'd be following and listening as I got to know them.

ctx.x: Did you go second lining, you follow, run after the first? I did the first line and the second line.

I don't know what the first line was, but we did it all. I used to tell my mother, because at that time we used to have the windows open. There wasn't no heck of it. We had the big fans. And I could, this is even before I started playing drums, I could feel to me, I could hear Paul Barber and Freddie Coleman, I don't know who they were, I used to see them as a kid, we all became good friends. I could hear boom, boom, boom. And I used to tell my mother, I said, my mother's a parade coming, she said, ain't no…
All these guys. He was a drummer at the palace? He was a drummer at the palace.
